nodes.impl: Candidate output is written to the run store and has no path to the Delivery Port. Promotion requires an agreement threshold sustained over a stated number of real runs, not a single good day.
nodes.full: Fixtures tell you a skill works on the cases someone thought of. Shadow running tells you what it does on the cases nobody thought of, at no risk to a client, which is the only honest way to gain confidence before a version handles work on its own.

nodes.label: Skill Registry & Versioning
nodes.plain: The only way a skill becomes live. Approval alone is not enough.
nodes.desc: Registers an approved skill at a specific version and publishes it into the Skill Index. Versions are immutable; a change is a new version and a new review.
nodes.impl: The single write path into the Skill Index. A SKILL.md sitting in a folder is not live — registration is a separate, recorded act.
nodes.full: Approval is a decision; registration is a deployment. Keeping them as two events means “someone approved this” and “this is running on client work” can never be the same moment by accident. This is the only edge from this column into the live system, and it carries a definition — never data, and never a client file.

nodes.label: Governance Record
nodes.plain: Every skill submitted, every decision, permanently.
nodes.desc: Append-only record of submissions, transcripts, decisions, reviewers and registered versions.
nodes.impl: Append-only store in a governance scope, separate from any engagement folder.
nodes.full: Answers the question a firm should always be able to answer about an automated system: what does it do, who decided it could, and when.

nodes.label: Event Bus
nodes.plain: Every node reports what it just did.
nodes.desc: Typed events from every step: skill.dispatched, mask.applied, guard.tieout.pass, hitl.item.queued, release.written. Guard passes are emitted, not only failures.
nodes.impl: Append-only event table plus an in-process publisher. Append-only is enforced three ways — no mutating method on the API, an ORM flush guard, and BEFORE UPDATE/BEFORE DELETE triggers on both backends, so the guarantee survives a psql prompt. Emission is fire-and-forget: a failure to record never fails a run, because observability must not become a new way for work to break. A malformed event still raises — that is a defect in the emitting node, not an infrastructure hiccup.
nodes.full: Emitting passes as well as failures is the point. A guard that only speaks up when it fires is indistinguishable, on a quiet day, from a guard that never ran at all.

nodes.label: Run Store
nodes.plain: The database behind everything the dashboard shows.
nodes.desc: Runs, steps, events, artifacts, costs, review items and decisions. The single source of truth for what happened.
nodes.impl: A repository behind a Protocol, chosen by one URL: SQLite locally through P24, Postgres after. Reads hand back frozen records rather than live ORM rows, so “the store is the source of truth” is a property of the store and not a request to callers. Also what the Analyst Chat reads, and what the Run Manifest is assembled from at the end of a run.
nodes.full: One store rather than logs scattered across services, because the question people actually ask — “what happened on the Henderson job on Tuesday?” — should be one query.

nodes.label: Checkpoint & Resume
nodes.plain: A crashed run resumes where it stopped, not from the beginning.
nodes.desc: Commits run state after every successfully completed step. On restart, completed steps are satisfied from the idempotency ledger and execution continues from the frontier.
nodes.impl: State is the compiled graph plus per-step results and status. Because steps are keyed and pure with respect to their inputs, resume is replay rather than reconstruction — there is no separate recovery code path to get wrong.
nodes.full: This matters more than it looks. Without it, a crash three quarters through a long run means paying again for every model call already made, and re-queuing every review item an analyst already answered — which is the fastest way to lose their willingness to use the thing.

nodes.label: Ops Console
nodes.plain: The always-on dashboard. What is running, right now.
nodes.desc: Live run feed, plan progress, per-skill trace, guard status strip, review inbox, cost meter, artifacts. Streams from the event bus.
nodes.impl: FastAPI + server-sent events to a browser client. A reader of the event bus — it holds no pipeline state and nothing depends on it. See the Ops Console tab for the mock.
nodes.full: Console down, runs continue. Run stalled, the console says so. Getting that dependency direction right is what makes it safe to have the dashboard always on.

nodes.label: Run Scorecard
nodes.plain: The verdict: did this run actually work, and against what bar?
nodes.desc: Computes a per-run verdict against declared acceptance criteria — document and period coverage, provenance completeness, tie-out agreement, conflicts resolved, residual masking, numeric integrity, budget, review outstanding, deliverable QC. Emits pass, pass with exceptions, halted, blocked or partial, and names every criterion that failed.
nodes.impl: Deterministic, computed from the event stream at end of run and written into the manifest (run_manifest@1.1.0: verdict, criteria version, every criterion’s measurement). The criteria live in ops/criteria/, one file per version, never edited in place, so “what counted as working” is answerable for a run from six months ago. Close-out checks the outcome a caller claims against the verdict the record supports and refuses a contradiction: clean is earned, not asserted. A criterion the record cannot measure is reported as such and keeps the verdict off pass — silence is never a pass.
nodes.full: Guards answer “did this particular check pass”. Nobody was answering “did the run work”, which left it a matter of opinion formed by scrolling a log. A run is not a boolean either — conflating halted before producing anything with delivered but three figures needed a person hides exactly the information a practice lead needs.

nodes.label: Analytics Dashboard
nodes.plain: Across all runs: is this working, and what should we fix?
nodes.desc: The aggregate view over every run. Outcome mix, first-pass yield, where runs stop, failures ranked by frequency and owner, autonomy and override trends against the human baseline, cost, and per-skill scorecards by scope.
nodes.impl: Reads the run store; holds no state of its own. Every panel is built to answer one question rather than to fill space — see the Console tab.
nodes.full: The live console answers “what is happening right now”. This answers the four questions that decide whether the project continues: is the system healthy, what should we fix first, is it getting better, and is anything stuck. Each of those has a number, and each number has the human baseline beside it — without which none of them mean anything.

nodes.label: Admin Console
nodes.plain: Where a person actually sets this thing up.
nodes.desc: The setup surface: environment and port bindings, watch locations, the active project roster, delivery destinations, the model bound to each practice area, preflight, and what an admin may and may not change.
nodes.impl: Reads and writes the Configuration Store and the Active Project Roster (admin/console.py); every write lands in the Config Change Log. It cannot reach a skill definition, a guard, or the live skills tree — those have their own governance chain — and where a method could be pushed past the line it refuses with CONFIG.ADMIN_FORBIDDEN: a review level is raised, never lowered; a budget sits at or below the firm ceiling; a credential’s presence is visible, never its value.
nodes.full: The system is designed to produce configuration failures — config is one of the six failure owners, described as “almost always a setup gap on a new engagement”. Until this tab existed there was nowhere for those failures to be prevented and nowhere for them to be fixed, which made the single most likely class of problem also the least served. Admin tab.

nodes.label: Setup Preflight
nodes.plain: Checks a setup before anyone relies on it — and says exactly what is wrong.
nodes.desc: Ten checks over a proposed or live configuration: path readable · credential present and unexpired · no two watches claiming one path · every active engagement has a resolving scope, a complete engagement profile, a template pin, a destination, a review policy and a budget · template hash matches the registered version · template declares every required input · destination writable · named recipe exists · headroom.
nodes.impl: Runs on demand and on every config write (admin/preflight.py). Emits the standard diagnostic — code, owner, expected, found, and what_now — with the owner set to config. A failing check blocks activation of that engagement rather than failing later inside a run: the console’s activate runs preflight for that engagement and refuses with every failing check, each a diagnostic. Not part of any run, so it emits into no event stream.
nodes.full: A setup error found here costs a minute. The same error found at run time costs a halted run, a diagnostic somebody has to read, and a client waiting. Deliberately not part of any run — it is a setup-time activity, so it never appears in a run’s event stream and never colours a node on the trace.

nodes.label: Config Change Log
nodes.plain: Who changed what, when, and why.
nodes.desc: Append-only record of every configuration change: the field, the old and new values, the person, the timestamp and a reason. Covers roster state changes, model rebindings, destination changes and credential rotations.
nodes.impl: Written by the Admin Console on every config write. Separate from the Run Manifest by necessity — configuration changes happen between runs, so no run record can hold them.
nodes.full: The most common real question after a surprising result is “what changed?”, and configuration is the likeliest answer. A run manifest can say which template version a deliverable used; only this can say that somebody repointed the practice group at a different model on Tuesday afternoon and why.

nodes.label: Token & Cost Meter
nodes.plain: What each run and each skill actually cost.
nodes.desc: Tokens and spend by run, by skill and by model tier, with a per-engagement rollup.
nodes.impl: Derived from usage on every model call. Tier choices on this map are cost decisions, and this is where they get checked against reality.
nodes.full: Without this, model tier selection is guesswork forever. With it, “does the classifier need to be mid tier?” is a question with a number attached.

nodes.label: Drift Monitor
nodes.plain: Watches whether a skill is quietly getting worse.
nodes.desc: Tracks human override rate, confidence distribution, guard failure rate and sampling-audit outcomes over time, per skill and per scope, alerting on a sustained move rather than a single bad run.
nodes.impl: Derived from the decision log and the event stream. A sustained rise in override rate opens a re-review on that skill in the governance chain — the outermost loop in the system.
nodes.full: Model providers update models. Clients change their chart of accounts. A skill edit has an effect nobody predicted. None announce themselves and none show in a single run. The override rate is the one number that moves when any of them does — and splitting it by scope matters, because the same skill can be healthy in non-ESOP work and degrading in ESOP work, which a single blended number would hide.

nodes.label: Stall & Alert Detection
nodes.plain: A run that goes quiet is a visible fact, not a mystery.
nodes.desc: Watches for steps exceeding expected duration, runs that stop emitting, repeated guard failures, and review items ageing past a threshold.
nodes.impl: Timer over the event stream. Alerts route to the console and, optionally, to a person.
nodes.full: The failure mode for an unattended pipeline is not a crash — a crash is loud. It is a run that silently stops and is noticed three days later when someone asks for the model.

nodes.label: Run Manifest
nodes.plain: The permanent record of one run, written at the end.
nodes.desc: Every source and its hash, every guard event including passes, every model and version used, every human decision, template version, coverage gaps, and total cost.
nodes.impl: Assembled from the run store at completion and written through the Delivery Port beside the deliverable. Append-only by convention; destination versioning gives immutability.
nodes.full: Written once at the end rather than maintained as live mutable state, which makes it a clean artifact rather than a thing that can be half-updated. It is also the answer to the question that actually gets asked in a review: what did the system check, on what sources, using which models, and what did it find.

nodes.label: Secrets Port
nodes.plain: Where credentials come from — .env today, a vault later.
nodes.desc: One interface for every credential: ShareFile key, Box credentials, database, model API key, mask vault encryption key.
nodes.impl: Protocol with implementations for env file, OS keyring and cloud secret managers. No credential is ever read directly from the environment by feature code.
nodes.full: Cheap to build now, and the single thing most likely to be hard-coded early and painful to unpick later.

nodes.label: LLM Provider Port
nodes.plain: Which model provider, behind one interface.
nodes.desc: Wraps model access so a provider change does not touch skill code. All calls pass the Outbound Payload Scan.
nodes.impl: Anthropic API by default; Bedrock or Vertex are configuration, not a rewrite. Model ids and versions are recorded per call for reproducibility.
nodes.full: Also the enforcement point for the first guarantee: because there is exactly one way to reach a model, there is exactly one place the payload scan has to sit.

nodes.label: Model & Prompt Pin
nodes.plain: Which exact model, effort setting and prompt version a run used.
nodes.desc: Pins model id, model version, effort level and prompt/skill version for the life of a run and records them in the manifest. A pinned model that is no longer available fails the run at startup rather than silently substituting a different one.
nodes.impl: Part of the plan hash. Upgrading a pin is a deliberate, reviewed change with a shadow run behind it. The low / mid / high tiers on this map resolve to concrete models — mapping and current rates on the Delivery tab.
nodes.full: Reproducibility is the point. A workfile that cannot say which model produced a figure is a workfile that cannot be defended, and silent provider-side substitution is the most common way that happens without anyone choosing it.

nodes.label: Job Queue Port
nodes.plain: How work gets scheduled.
nodes.desc: Job submission, retry and status behind one interface.
nodes.impl: In-process for local runs; Redis + RQ for a server; a managed queue in a cloud. Same interface throughout.
nodes.full: Phase 1 needs no queue at all. Having the interface from the start means adding one later is not a refactor of the pipeline.

nodes.label: Compute Target
nodes.plain: Runs as a container. Anywhere that runs containers works.
nodes.desc: One Docker image, driven by config. No managed-service primitive is depended on anywhere in the code.
nodes.impl: Local process, Docker, or any container host — Azure Container Apps, ECS, Cloud Run, on-prem. The deployment choice is an environment, not an architecture.
nodes.full: The project context is explicit that no work-sanctioned cloud exists yet. The only responsible response is to make that decision reversible, and containers plus ports is the cheapest way to do it.

invariants.t: No model node can reach the Mask Vault. Re-identification is deterministic code, so a token can never be resolved by something that might guess.
Every payload bound for a model passes through one door, so there is exactly one place to check what leaves and one place to record it.
Only CODE nodes touch re-identification. No skill has an unmask tool — it is the one step where a plausible mistake is indistinguishable from correctness.
Every figure in a deliverable cleared Provenance and was recomputed by Tie-Out.
A generative step may render a verified figure but can never originate or alter one — the narrative is written after the numbers are locked, and its schema has no field a figure can enter through.

One node releases client work, with one inbound edge. The run manifest is written separately and unconditionally — including when a run halts. Configuration selects the destination but carries no content — only a flow edge can move an artifact.
Governance never reads client-identifying data — only masked payloads — and its one edge back into the live system publishes a skill definition, never a file.
Every guard writes to the record — passes included, so silence is never ambiguous.
Only a human decision can write to the Precedent Store, so the system never learns from itself unchecked.
Nothing runs unscoped, and never two runs at once on one deal.
Every loop is declared with a maximum iteration count. The compiler rejects any cycle that is not one.
Every step is keyed and idempotent, so a retry, a resume and a manual re-run are the same operation.
Every run records the exact model, prompt, skill, template, taxonomy and schema versions it used.
A scope overlay can only tighten. Nothing deeper in the tree can loosen a review requirement or a privacy class.
An engagement can only see the skills its scope resolves to. A Corporate Finance skill is not declined by an ESOP run — it was never in it.
Precedents are retrieved only from the engagement’s own scope, and a repeat client sees its own prior decisions first.
Every tool call is authorised before it executes. No skill can reach a tool around the gate.
Everything a model is shown is assembled in one place and recorded, so any call can be reconstructed exactly.
Every run ends with a computed verdict against versioned criteria. No run’s outcome is a matter of opinion.
Every failure carries a stable code, an owner and what to do next. A message nobody can act on is a defect.
A dropped draft is a candidate, not a skill. No path from the drop folder to the tree skips fixtures, review or a shadow run.
Nothing reaches the Skill Index without passing fixtures and a shadow run first.
No configuration edge reaches a node that can fail closed. Config writes the engagement record; guards read the run.
An engagement not on the roster has no path from any intake source into the pipeline. Inactive is unreachable, not merely unchecked.
Every active engagement resolves to exactly one delivery destination and exactly one model template pin.
